text.p: Bausch & Lomb Inc is comfortable with analysts' concensus estimate that the company will earn $2.25 per share in 1997, Senior Vice-President of Finance Stephen McCluski said Thursday.
But he told a Dillon Read analyst meeting that the company's eyewear business, which included brands like Ray Ban, continued to be a slight drag on financial performance.
"The eyewear business faced challenges in 1996 and these are still a factor today," McCluski said.
Bausch & Lomb is in the midst of a strategic restructuring to shift its focus from diversified health care optics to eye care.
It has said it expects annual savings of over $100 million in 1999 because of the plan.
Initiatives to bolster Bausch & Lomb's eyewear unit included transforming product delivery capabilities, outsourcing more products and improving the manufacturing process, McCluski said.
"Over the next three years, our goal for eyewear is to see a steady improvement in revenue growth to about 10 percent," he said. "We are looking for operating margins to improve to the mid-teens."
The restructuring would also benefit the company's vision care unit, which accounted for about half of Bausch & Lomb's revenues, he said.

"Over the next three years," McCluski said, "the company's goal is to accelerate revenue growth for this division from the eight to 10 percent range to the 10 to 12 percent range, while keeping operating margins at 20 to 21 percent."
